learn.b: Hangul letters are easy: each letter has one sound. Letters are stacked into square blocks, one block per syllable. The basic vowels are ㅏ (a), ㅓ (eo), ㅗ (o), ㅜ (u), ㅡ (eu), and ㅣ (i).
Add a short line to make a y sound. ㅑ (ya), ㅕ (yeo), ㅛ (yo), and ㅠ (yu). The vowels ㅐ (ae) and ㅔ (e) are written differently but sound almost the same today.
A syllable cannot start with a vowel alone, so we write a silent ㅇ first. 아 (a), 어 (eo), 오 (o), 우 (u), 으 (eu), 이 (i). Tall vowels like ㅏ and ㅣ go on the right. Flat vowels like ㅗ and ㅜ go below.

qs.why: The silent ㅇ plus ㅗ (o) gives 'o'.

qs.why: ㅑ is ㅏ with an extra line, so it is 'ya'.

qs.why: Flat vowels such as ㅗ, ㅜ, and ㅡ are written under the consonant.

qs.q: In the block 아 (a), the letter ㅇ at the start makes a sound.
qs.why: At the start of a block, ㅇ is silent.

learn.b: ㄱ (g or k), ㄴ (n), ㄷ (d or t), ㄹ (r or l), ㅁ (m), ㅂ (b or p), ㅅ (s), ㅈ (j), and ㅎ (h). The letter ㅇ is silent at the start of a block.
ㅋ (k), ㅌ (t), ㅍ (p), and ㅊ (ch) are the strong versions with a puff of air. Double letters like ㄲ (kk), ㄸ (tt), ㅃ (pp), ㅆ (ss), and ㅉ (jj) are tight and tense.
Put a consonant and a vowel together: 가 (ga), 나 (na), 마 (ma), 바 (ba), 고 (go). A consonant can also sit at the bottom as a final sound. 한 (han) ends in ㄴ. 밥 (bap) ends in ㅂ. 물 (mul) ends in ㄹ.

네 (ne) means yes and 아니요 (aniyo) means no. Say 안녕히 가세요 (annyeonghi gaseyo) to someone who is leaving. Say 안녕히 계세요 (annyeonghi gyeseyo) to someone who is staying.
Say 저는 민입니다 (jeoneun Min-imnida) for I am Min. 만나서 반갑습니다 (mannaseo bangapseumnida) means nice to meet you.

learn.b: These numbers are used for dates, money, and phone numbers. 일 (il) is 1, 이 (i) is 2, 삼 (sam) is 3, 사 (sa) is 4, 오 (o) is 5. 육 (yuk) is 6, 칠 (chil) is 7, 팔 (pal) is 8, 구 (gu) is 9, 십 (sip) is 10.
These numbers are used for counting things and for age. 하나 (hana) is 1, 둘 (dul) is 2, and 셋 (set) is 3.
엄마 (eomma) is mom and 아빠 (appa) is dad. 동생 (dongsaeng) is a younger brother or sister. 가족 (gajok) means family.

Say 물 주세요 (mul juseyo) for Please give me water. 맛있어요 (masisseoyo) means delicious. 좋아해요 (joahaeyo) means like.

learn.b: 이에요 (ieyo) or 예요 (yeyo) means is or am. 학생이에요 (haksaengieyo) means I am a student. Use 이에요 after a consonant and 예요 after a vowel.
있어요 (isseoyo) means have or there is. 없어요 (eopseoyo) means do not have or there is not.
가요 (gayo) means go and 와요 (wayo) means come. Put 안 (an) before a verb to make it negative. 안 먹어요 (an meogeoyo) means do not eat.

learn.b: 은 (eun) or 는 (neun) marks the topic. Use 는 after a vowel and 은 after a consonant. 저는 (jeoneun) means as for me. 도 (do) means also: 저도 (jeodo) means me too.

을 (eul) or 를 (reul) marks the thing that receives the action. Use 를 after a vowel and 을 after a consonant. 사과를 먹어요 (sagwareul meogeoyo) means I eat an apple. 밥을 먹어요 (babeul meogeoyo) means I eat rice.

에 (e) means to a place or at a time: 학교에 가요 (hakgyoe gayo) means I go to school. 에서 (eseo) means at a place where you do an action: 도서관에서 공부해요 (doseogwaneseo gongbuhaeyo) means I study at the library.

qs.why: 밥을 marks rice as the object of 먹어요.

learn.b: 월요일 (woryoil) is Monday, 화요일 (hwayoil) is Tuesday, 수요일 (suyoil) is Wednesday, and 목요일 (mogyoil) is Thursday. 금요일 (geumyoil) is Friday, 토요일 (toyoil) is Saturday, and 일요일 (iryoil) is Sunday.
For hours use the native numbers plus 시 (si): 한 시 (han si) is 1 o'clock, 두 시 (du si) is 2, 세 시 (se si) is 3. For minutes use Sino-Korean numbers plus 분 (bun): 삼십 분 (samsip bun) is 30 minutes.

몇 시예요 (myeot siyeyo) means What time is it? Answer 세 시예요 (se siyeyo) for It is three o'clock. 지금 (jigeum) means now. Parts of the day: 아침 (achim) morning, 점심 (jeomsim) noon or lunch, 저녁 (jeonyeok) evening, 밤 (bam) night.

learn.b: 빨간색 (ppalgansaek) is red, 파란색 (paransaek) is blue, 노란색 (noransaek) is yellow, and 초록색 (choroksaek) is green. 검은색 (geomeunsaek) is black and 흰색 (huinsaek) is white.
Describing words end like verbs. 커요 (keoyo) means big and 작아요 (jagayo) means small. 예뻐요 (yeppeoyo) means pretty. 좋아요 (joayo) means good and 나빠요 (nappayo) means bad.
Put the describing word last. 이 사과는 커요 (i sagwaneun keoyo) means This apple is big. Add 정말 (jeongmal) for really: 정말 예뻐요 (jeongmal yeppeoyo) means really pretty.

공부해요 (gongbuhaeyo) means study. 일해요 (ilhaeyo) means work. 자요 (jayo) means sleep. 저는 집에서 자요 (jeoneun jibeseo jayo) means I sleep at home.

learn.b: Add 았어요 or 었어요 (asseoyo or eosseoyo) to the verb stem. 먹다 (meokda) becomes 먹었어요 (meogeosseoyo), which means ate. 가다 (gada) becomes 갔어요 (gasseoyo), which means went.
Put 안 (an) before the past verb. 안 갔어요 (an gasseoyo) means did not go.
어제 (eoje) means yesterday and 오늘 (oneul) means today. 내일 (naeil) means tomorrow. 지난주 (jinanju) means last week.

learn.b: Add ㄹ 거예요 (l geoyeyo) after a vowel stem and 을 거예요 (eul geoyeyo) after a consonant stem. 가다 becomes 갈 거예요 (gal geoyeyo), will go. 먹다 becomes 먹을 거예요 (meogeul geoyeyo), will eat. 하다 becomes 할 거예요 (hal geoyeyo), will do.
내일 (naeil) is tomorrow. 주말 (jumal) is weekend. 다음 주 (daeum ju) is next week. 다음 달 (daeum dal) is next month. 계획 (gyehoek) means plan.
주말에 뭐 할 거예요 (jumare mwo hal geoyeyo) means What will you do on the weekend? Answer 친구를 만날 거예요 (chingureul mannal geoyeyo), I will meet a friend. 만나다 (mannada) means to meet.

learn.b: Add (으)세요 (euseyo) to a verb stem for a polite command. 가세요 (gaseyo) means please go. 오세요 (oseyo) means please come. 앉으세요 (anjeuseyo) means please sit. 보세요 (boseyo) means please look.
Add 아/어 주세요 (a/eo juseyo) to ask someone to do something for you. 도와 주세요 (dowa juseyo) means please help me. 다시 말해 주세요 (dasi malhae juseyo) means please say it again. 천천히 (cheoncheonhi) means slowly.
Add 지 마세요 (ji maseyo) to a verb stem to say do not. 가지 마세요 (gaji maseyo) means do not go. 걱정하지 마세요 (geokjeonghaji maseyo) means do not worry. 잠깐만요 (jamkkanmanyo) means just a moment.

learn.b: Add (으)ㄹ 수 있어요 (eul su isseoyo) to say can. 한국어를 할 수 있어요 (hangugeoreul hal su isseoyo) means I can speak Korean. Use 수 없어요 (su eopseoyo) for cannot. 수영할 수 있어요 (suyeonghal su isseoyo) means I can swim.
Put 못 (mot) before a verb for cannot. 못 가요 (mot gayo) means I cannot go. 못 먹어요 (mot meogeoyo) means I cannot eat.

아/어도 돼요 (a/eodo dwaeyo) means it is okay to. 먹어도 돼요 (meogeodo dwaeyo)? means May I eat? (으)면 안 돼요 (myeon an dwaeyo) means must not. 사진 (sajin) is photo: 사진을 찍어도 돼요 (sajineul jjigeodo dwaeyo) means May I take a photo?

의사 (uisa) is doctor, 약 (yak) is medicine, and 약국 (yakguk) is pharmacy. 많이 (mani) means a lot. 머리가 많이 아파요 (meoriga mani apayo) means My head hurts a lot.

비가 와요 (biga wayo) means it rains. 눈이 와요 (nuni wayo) means it snows. 바람이 불어요 (barami bureoyo) means the wind blows. 우산 (usan) is umbrella.
봄 (bom) is spring, 여름 (yeoreum) is summer, 가을 (gaeul) is autumn, and 겨울 (gyeoul) is winter. 여름에는 더워요 (yeoreumeneun deowoyo) means It is hot in summer.

learn.b: 보다 (boda) means than. 이것이 저것보다 비싸요 (igeosi jeogeotboda bissayo) means This is more expensive than that. 더 (deo) means more: 더 싸요 (deo ssayo) means cheaper.
가장 (gajang) and 제일 (jeil) both mean the most. 이 음식을 가장 좋아해요 (i eumsigeul gajang joahaeyo) means I like this food the most. 같이 (gachi) means together.

Add ㄴ 적이 있어요 (n jeogi isseoyo) after a vowel stem to say I have done it before. 한국에 간 적이 있어요 (hanguge gan jeogi isseoyo) means I have been to Korea. After a consonant use 은 적이 있어요: 먹은 적이 있어요 (meogeun jeogi isseoyo). 처음 (cheoeum) means first time.

learn.b: ا (alif) is a long 'ā'. ب (bāʾ) is 'b'. ت (tāʾ) is 't'. ث (thāʾ) is 'th' as in think. ج (jīm) is 'j'. ح (ḥāʾ) is a strong breathy 'h'. خ (khāʾ) is 'kh', like the ch in Scottish loch.
د (dāl) is 'd'. ذ (dhāl) is 'dh' as in this. ر (rāʾ) is a rolled 'r'. ز (zayn) is 'z'. س (sīn) is 's'. ش (shīn) is 'sh'. ص (ṣād) is a heavy, deep 's'.

Arabic is written from right to left, and letters join in a word. Each letter changes shape a little at the start, middle, or end. Six letters never join to the next one: ا د ذ ر ز و. The word باب (bāb) means door.

qs.why: ا is one of the six letters that do not join forward.

learn.b: ض (ḍād) is a heavy 'd'. ط (ṭāʾ) is a heavy 't'. ظ (ẓāʾ) is a heavy 'dh'. ع (ʿayn) is a sound from deep in the throat. غ (ghayn) is like a gargle 'gh'. ف (fāʾ) is 'f'. ق (qāf) is a deep 'q'.
ك (kāf) is 'k'. ل (lām) is 'l'. م (mīm) is 'm'. ن (nūn) is 'n'. ه (hāʾ) is 'h'. و (wāw) is 'w' or a long 'ū'. ي (yāʾ) is 'y' or a long 'ī'. That makes 28 letters.

Short vowels are small marks above or below a letter. Fatḥa ـَ is 'a', kasra ـِ is 'i', and ḍamma ـُ is 'u'. So بَ is ba, بِ is bi, and بُ is bu. Sukūn ـْ means no vowel. Most texts leave them out. The word كتاب (kitāb) means book.

Which letter makes the 'f' sound?
qs.why: ف has one dot above and is 'f'.

qs.why: The small mark under the letter is kasra, which is 'i'.

شكرا (shukran) means thank you and عفوا (ʿafwan) means you're welcome. نعم (naʿam) is yes and لا (lā) is no. Say اسمي (ismī) and your name for my name is.

In Arabic the describing word comes after the noun. بيت كبير (bayt kabīr) means a big house. For a feminine noun like سيارة, add ة to the adjective: سيارة كبيرة (sayyāra kabīra) means a big car. أحب (uḥibb) means I like.

صباحا (ṣabāḥan) means in the morning and مساء (masāʾan) means in the evening. الآن (al-ān) means now. يوم (yawm) is day, أسبوع (usbūʿ) is week, and شهر (shahr) is month.

learn.b: هذا (hādhā) means this for a masculine noun: هذا كتاب (hādhā kitāb) means this is a book. هذه (hādhihi) is for a feminine noun: هذه سيارة (hādhihi sayyāra) means this is a car. الـ (al-) means the: الكتاب (al-kitāb) is the book.
Add ـي (-ī) to a noun for my: كتابي (kitābī) is my book and بيتي (baytī) is my house. Add ـك (-ka) for your (male): كتابك (kitābuk) is your book.
عندي (ʿindī) means I have. عندي كتاب (ʿindī kitāb) means I have a book. عندك (ʿindak) means you have. Say ليس عندي (laysa ʿindī) for I do not have: ليس عندي سيارة (laysa ʿindī sayyāra).

learn.b: The present tense adds a prefix to the verb. أ (a) is I, ن (n) is we, ي (y) is he, and ت (t) is she or you. From درس (study): أدرس (adrus) I study, ندرس (nadrus) we study, يدرس (yadrus) he studies, تدرس (tadrus) she studies.
أستيقظ (astayqiẓ) means I wake up. أعمل (aʿmal) means I work. أنام (anām) means I sleep. أذهب إلى العمل (adhhab ilā l-ʿamal) means I go to work.
دائما (dāʾiman) means always. أحيانا (aḥyānan) means sometimes. يوميا (yawmiyyan) means daily. Use لا (lā) before the verb for not: لا أدرس (lā adrus) means I do not study.

غدا (ghadan) is tomorrow. الأسبوع القادم (al-usbūʿ al-qādim) is next week. عطلة (ʿuṭla) is holiday. أخطط (ukhaṭṭiṭ) means I plan.

سأسافر (sa-usāfir) means I will travel. سأزور (sa-azūr) means I will visit. سأزور أصدقائي غدا (sa-azūr aṣdiqāʾī ghadan) means I will visit my friends tomorrow. Add إن شاء الله (in shāʾa llāh) for God willing.

يمين (yamīn) is right and يسار (yasār) is left. مباشرة (mubāsharatan) means straight ahead. انعطف (inʿaṭif) means turn.
مستشفى (mustashfā) is hospital, محطة (maḥaṭṭa) is station, and بنك (bank) is bank. قريب (qarīb) means near and بعيد (baʿīd) means far.

learn.b: بكم (bikam) means How much? غالٍ (ghālin) means expensive and رخيص (rakhīṣ) means cheap.
تذكرة (tadhkira) is ticket, فندق (funduq) is hotel, and جواز سفر (jawāz safar) is passport. قطار (qiṭār) is train and طائرة (ṭāʾira) is plane.
أريد (urīd) means I want. أريد تذكرة (urīd tadhkira) means I want a ticket. أشتري (ashtarī) means I buy.

learn.b: رأس (raʾs) is head, عين (ʿayn) is eye, يد (yad) is hand, رجل (rijl) is leg or foot, بطن (baṭn) is stomach, فم (fam) is mouth, أنف (anf) is nose, and أذن (udhun) is ear.

أشعر بألم في (ashʿur bi-alam fī) means I feel pain in. أشعر بألم في رأسي (ashʿur bi-alam fī raʾsī) means I feel pain in my head. عندي صداع (ʿindī ṣudāʿ) means I have a headache. عندي حمى (ʿindī ḥumma) means I have a fever. مريض (marīḍ) means sick.
طبيب (ṭabīb) is doctor, صيدلية (ṣaydaliyya) is pharmacy, and دواء (dawāʾ) is medicine. أحتاج إلى طبيب (aḥtāj ilā ṭabīb) means I need a doctor.

learn.b: الطقس (aṭ-ṭaqs) means weather. حار (ḥārr) is hot, بارد (bārid) is cold, مشمس (mushmis) is sunny, غائم (ghāʾim) is cloudy, and ممطر (mumṭir) is rainy.
مطر (maṭar) is rain, شمس (shams) is sun, ثلج (thalj) is snow, and ريح (rīḥ) is wind. كيف الطقس اليوم (kayfa aṭ-ṭaqs al-yawm) means How is the weather today?

الربيع (ar-rabīʿ) is spring, الصيف (aṣ-ṣayf) is summer, الخريف (al-kharīf) is autumn, and الشتاء (ash-shitāʾ) is winter. الجو بارد في الشتاء (al-jaww bārid fī ash-shitāʾ) means The weather is cold in winter.

learn.b: من فضلك أعطني (min faḍlik aʿṭinī) means please give me. ساعدني (sāʿidnī) means help me. هل يمكنني الجلوس هنا (hal yumkinunī al-julūs hunā) means Can I sit here?
أستطيع (astaṭīʿ) means I can. أستطيع أن أتكلم العربية (astaṭīʿ an atakallam al-ʿarabiyya) means I can speak Arabic. لا أستطيع (lā astaṭīʿ) means I cannot.
يجب (yajib) means must. يجب أن أذهب (yajib an adhhab) means I must go. أريد أن (urīd an) means I want to. أريد أن أسافر (urīd an usāfir) means I want to travel.

learn.b: ممتع (mumtiʿ) means fun or enjoyable and ممل (mumill) means boring. صعب (ṣaʿb) means difficult and سهل (sahl) means easy.
أعتقد (aʿtaqid) means I think. أعتقد أنه ممتع (aʿtaqid annahu mumtiʿ) means I think it is fun. أحب (uḥibb) means I like.
لماذا (limādhā) means why and لأن (li-anna) means because. لكن (lākin) means but.

learn.b: To compare, use a form like أكبر (akbar), bigger, with من (min), than. القاهرة أكبر من روما (al-Qāhira akbar min Rūmā) means Cairo is bigger than Rome. أصغر (aṣghar) is smaller, أجمل (ajmal) is more beautiful, and أسهل (ashal) is easier.
أرخص (arkhaṣ) is cheaper and أغلى (aghlā) is more expensive. أصعب (aṣʿab) is harder. أفضل (afḍal) means better or best. أكثر (akthar) means more.
زرت (zurtu) means I visited. زرت إيطاليا من قبل (zurtu Īṭāliyā min qabl) means I have visited Italy before. من قبل (min qabl) means before. لم أزر (lam azur) means I have not visited.

qs.why: أكبر is bigger and من means than.
